title: Tigers’ Justin Verlander scratched from long-awaited return start with left hamstring injury
content:
DETROIT — Justin Verlander’s long-anticipated return to the Tigers’ rotation will have to wait.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch announced Friday that the team has scratched Verlander from his scheduled start Sunday at Comerica Park. Right-hander Keider Montero is expected to pitch in Verlander’s place.

Verlander, who had been on the 60-day injured list with left hip inflammation, reported a separate issue with his left hamstring after throwing a bullpen Wednesday in Houston. Further evaluation discovered a strain in Verlander’s hamstring, leading to the decision to shut him down.

“This is not a matter of days,” Hinch said. “It’s a matter of weeks. We’re going to need a full rehab process to get him back to throwing again. Obviously, frustrating news for him and for us, given the excitement that was building around his start on Sunday.”

The Tigers signed the 43-year-old Verlander to a one-year, $13 million contract this winter, hoping for an emotional homecoming to the franchise where Verlander spent the first 13 seasons of his MLB career.

Verlander, though, has made only one start this season, giving up five earned runs in 3 2/3 innings on March 30 in Arizona. Verlander ended up scratched from his next start, which was supposed to be his first outing as a Tiger at Comerica Park since Aug. 20, 2017.

The hip issue lingered and led to a long recovery. Just as Verlander was preparing to return to the majors after two rehab starts and a handful of live bullpen sessions, the hamstring injury flared up and cast more uncertainty over what was supposed to be a storybook season.

“Glass half full, I get back to throwing, and this thing heals up, and it’s like, ‘Oh, wow, this was something that also was kind of lingering, and now I’m better than I was before,’” Verlander said. “But it still doesn’t take the sting away from being tantalizingly close to finally being back on the mound here at home and having it pulled out from under me.”
